questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The study destination had to be an english-speaking country since I wanted to improve my English skills. Also, Australia has been on my bucket list for many years and I thought an exchange program would be a great opportunity to explore the country and its culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was hard to navigate in the different systems but overall it was ok.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not a lot

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Not much assistance was provided. You have to seek information about everything yourself and be prepared to spend a lot of time doing so.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, but I was also lucky to know someone who had been on exchange in Sydney before so I could stay with her old roommate. My friends who stayed off campus didn't have much trouble finding housing either. My impression is that it's easier finding housing in Sydney than in Copenhagen, but it's a bit more expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend it if you want to live closer to the city. The on-campus housing is a bit far from the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It looked dirty and messy but I think it's very nice that it's an option since it provides exchange students with safety in terms of housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Macquaire University has a super confusing registration system. Very hard to navigate in.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After you get your courses preapproved by KU you need to apply for a special waiver at MQ (if you haven't done the prerequisites). This process was super frustrating and it was impossible to get help from MQ. On their website they say that it takes 7-10 days to get a special waiver. I waited for 2 months. When I tried to call and email them, they just replied that it was a mistake but they didn't know what to do. I got the special waivers the day before my courses begun which was way to late since I had no time to prepare for my courses. If they hadn't been approved I wouldn't have time to request new ones either. Overall a bad experience and a very stressful start.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Macquaire University help center. Consisted of students who couldn't assist properly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted but it was a frustrating process with little help.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: make sure to have a lot of backup courses pre-approved by KU.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: courses were good

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: less self-study and more about participating in the tutorials.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Strategic Management, counselling approaches and principles, research methods in psychology, and Indigenous queer theory and practice.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: all of them, they were interesting!

questions.answer: Transportation was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't participate much in the non-academic opportunities but my impression is that there were a lot!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many clubs were available

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend doing an effort to meet a lot of people in the beginning and do a lot of social things together to establish a network in Sydney. Otherwise it can get lonely being that far away for half a year I think. Fortunately a lot of students from KU goes to Sydney for exchange which makes it super easy to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I spend my time sightseeing, going to museums or clubs.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - I think that Australians are very kind and chatty and makes you feel welcome.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You have to make an active effort in order to socializing with local students. It's easier to socialize with other Danes to be honest.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The most challenging part was adjusting to a different school system, but I learned a lot from that which I'm grateful for.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: it's such an interesting culture with a complicated story. I think my favorite part was that so may sub-cultures existed side-by-side in Sydney.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) be prepared to not get a lot of help in regard to courses from the host institution. Have a lot of backup courses ready. 
2) The professors are very dedicated which makes the different courses interesting. The academic level is high which is nice. 
3) You will meet so many other exchange students there so don't stress about being alone in Sydney. You won't be.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of any

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: getting to know the culture, seeing Australia, and meeting so many amazing people. It has been one of the best experiences I've ever had and I would do it again without hesitation.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The registration process at the host institution.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
